item.title: AI and Global Food Security: A Focus on Food Systems
item.description: As food systems face increasingly severe and complex shocks, AI-enabled innovations are proliferating across food production, logistics, markets, and humanitarian response. CSIS experts unpack the challenges and opportunities of AI for global food systems.

item.title: Rice at a Crossroads: Rethinking Japan’s Food Security
item.description: To ensure national food self-sufficiency in times of crisis while keeping prices affordable for consumers, Japan must strengthen its agricultural production capacity by better managing farmland, creating safety nets for farmers, and adopting cost-saving technologies.

item.title: Fueling Vulnerability: The Economic and Strategic Costs of Oil Dependence in the Pacific
item.description: Pacific Island economies face a double exposure: weaker growth in major partners and global oil shocks. Higher fuel prices linked to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz could cut GDP by several percentage points and deepen reliance on outside powers.

item.title: The Presidential Memo on Combating Transnational Cybercrime: Implications for Industry and Government
item.description: The Trump administration has directed the private sector to conduct offensive cyber operations in cyberspace. This move was long expected and sends an important signal to adversaries that the United States is hardening its posture against adversaries in cyberspace. But much will depend on its implementation and ensuring clear alignment with private sector risk appetites.

item.title: Open for Business
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East spotlights growing trade volumes between Syria and select countries or regions since the fall of Assad and the lifting of sanctions.

item.title: Iran can’t have nuclear weapons but North Korea can? There’s logic here.
item.description: There’s real logic beneath Trump’s split nuclear strategy. Iran and North Korea present very different nonproliferation problems.

item.title: There’s Real Logic Beneath Trump’s Split Nuclear Strategy
item.description: As President Trump moves in opposite directions on Iran and North Korea’s nuclear programs, CSIS's Victor Cha unpacks the split nuclear strategy in the Washington Post.

item.title: The Emperor’s Wardrobe Malfunction
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch argues that countries have begun adapting to the Trump administration’s trade policy by pursuing nonbinding agreements that offer immediate appeasement but provide limited enforceability.
